clue.text: Solvers slightly confused about working author producing novel

indicators.note: about tells us the rearranged word goes round the other pieces, enclosing them
the solvers are only mildly muddled, so their letters are lightly rearranged, here just one letter shifting place

parts.note: working means on, as a machine that is on
George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

explanation.surface: Puzzle solvers, a little bewildered, are puzzling over a writer at work on a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly confused' shifts just one letter to make SLOVERS, and 'about' wraps it round the two pieces. George Sand was the pen name of a French woman novelist; the book is D. H. Lawrence's.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is D. H. Lawrence's 1913 autobiographical book, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Modern poet with doubtful reputation

definitions.meaning: Dylan, the twentieth-century Welsh poet, bore this surname
the apostle who doubted the Resurrection gave the phrase for a habitual sceptic, one with a doubter's reputation

explanation.definitionFit: Dylan the Welsh poet shares the name with the doubting apostle, whose name became a byword for a sceptic.

clue.text: Club game in historic Shropshire village

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A golfer's club and a card game are on offer in a historic English village.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county; the village takes its name from the world's first cast-iron bridge, built there in 1779.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shropshire village is named after its famous eighteenth-century metal span over the Severn, a cradle of the Industrial Revolution.

clue.text: Bachelor getting a ring for movie actress

parts.note: to ring someone is to give them a call

explanation.surface: A single man gets engaged to a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a wedding band in the surface, but it means a telephone call. Lauren Bacall starred in Hollywood films of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren, the Hollywood star of To Have and Have Not, is an example of a film actress.

clue.text: See 7
Unproductive inclination

definitions.meaning: ... years or ... land yield little, so the word means meagre or unfruitful
to tilt or slope is to incline, and a slant of that kind is the second sense

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means meagre or unfruitful, while the noun or verb sense is a tilt or slant from upright.

clue.text: A celeb in a war for a moving picture shot by 17 6

indicators.note: moving sets the letters in motion so that they come out in a new arrangement

parts.words: A celeb in a war for a

explanation.surface: A celebrity caught up in a war appears in a motion picture made by a director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving picture' reads as one phrase, but 'moving' is the anagram signal on A CELEB IN A WAR FOR A. 17 6 is DAVID LEAN, who directed the 1962 film.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lean directed the 1962 epic about T. E. Lawrence in the desert, so it is a film he shot.

clue.text: Driver and conductor

definitions.meaning: a driver is a golf club, and some long clubs are of this type
Sir Henry, founder of the Proms concerts, was a famous conductor

explanation.definitionFit: Long golf clubs, drivers included, are called by this name, and Sir Henry of that name conducted the London Proms.

clue.text: Partner found where the opposing team lines up

definitions.meaning: a spouse is jokingly called one's better or ...

definitions.text: where the opposing team lines up
definitions.meaning: in a football match the opponents occupy the ... of the pitch

explanation.definitionFit: A spouse or partner is colloquially one's other half, and a rival side lines up in the half of the pitch that is not yours.

clue.text: Source of poetic inspiration among liberators

indicators.note: among says the answer is a run of letters sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A poet finds inspiration among freedom fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, and the Muses were the sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Simpleton without penny, a hindrance for him

definitions.text: Simpleton without penny, a hindrance for him

indicators.note: without tells us the following pieces are taken away from the word before it

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in the legal phrase without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: A fool with no money finds that his lack of cash holds him back.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Simple Simon cannot buy a pie because he has no penny, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme simpleton met a pieman but had no money, so his poverty stopped him getting a pie.

clue.text: Biblical plant providing title for 17 21 7

definitions.meaning: in the Book of Numbers the staff of Moses' brother miraculously sprouted and bore almonds
17 21 7 is David Herbert Lawrence, whose 1922 novel bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: The miraculously budding staff in Numbers, also a garden flower's name, gave D. H. Lawrence the title of a 1922 novel.

clue.text: Prodigal son Walter excitedly embraces

indicators.note: embraces says the rearranged name wraps around another piece
when Walter acts excitedly his letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Walter gives the returning prodigal son a warm hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges the name into WATREL, and 'embraces' takes in the S. 'Prodigal son' looks like one phrase from the parable, but only 'Prodigal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A prodigal is someone who squanders money, which is exactly what a spendthrift good-for-nothing does.

clue.text: Having diameter internally as measure of distance

indicators.note: internally tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: having means with, as in a man having a hat is a man with a hat

explanation.surface: Something with a diameter inside it serves as a way to measure distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth from side to side is a measurement of extent, a distance across something.

clue.text: Philosopher-king is such a pig

parts.note: Francis Bacon was an English philosopher and statesman
ER is the Latin abbreviation Edwardus Rex, for King Edward

explanation.surface: A thinker who is also a monarch turns out to be a swine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philosopher-king' suggests Plato's ideal ruler, but the hyphenated term splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig fattened to be cured as bacon is a specific term for such an animal raised for the table.

clue.text: See 27
Manages to protect one in financial collapses

indicators.note: to protect something is to shelter it, so the word for manages goes round the other piece

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A manager tries to shield someone from economic disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankruptcies and financial disasters are commonly described as people's or firms' utter downfall in the plural.

clue.text: French artist a saint? Not from what we hear

definitions.meaning: Jacques-Louis, the French neoclassical painter of The Death of Marat
the patron saint of Wales shares the name, though not the French pronunciation

explanation.surface: A French painter is wrongly thought holy because of how his name sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not from what we hear' warns that the two senses are pronounced differently: the French painter's name is said da-VEED, the Welsh saint's DAY-vid.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques-Louis of this surname painted for Napoleon, and the patron saint of Wales bears the same name, spelt identically.

clue.text: Pigment — one imported by long-lasting ruler over unsettled India

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above, so before, the second
imported by says the piece is brought inside the other one

parts.note: VR stands for Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria, who reigned for over 63 years
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: unsettled India is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the country's name supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pigment was brought in by a monarch with a long reign who ruled over a troubled India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imported by' places the numeral inside the royal cipher, 'unsettled' makes IDIAN, and 'over' sets the first piece above the second in this down clue. Victoria reigned for 63 years.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bluish-green chromium oxide pigment used by artists, so it is a kind of paint colouring.

clue.text: One end of parsnip, say, or other vegetable

indicators.note: say tells us the letter is to be spoken and heard rather than read
one end of parsnip points to its opening letter

explanation.surface: Asking about one end of a parsnip, or else a different vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter P, spoken aloud, is identical in sound to the small green legume, a vegetable other than the parsnip.
explanation.definitionFit: The small round green seed is a common vegetable, different from the parsnip in the surface.

clue.text: Light musical work only one person can play

definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of 1881 bears this name
solitaire, the card game for a single player, is known by this name in Britain

explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operetta shares its name with the British term for solitaire, a card game for one.

clue.text: A private room I provided for Arab citizen

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat

explanation.surface: A private room is provided for someone from Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: The citizen comes from Aden, a port city in Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Aden, the port city of southern Yemen on the Arabian peninsula, is a citizen of an Arab city.

clue.text: Metaphysical poet queen included in her speculation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: included in tells us the queen goes inside the gamble

parts.note: a bet is a gamble or speculation
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A poet is caught up in her financial gamble with a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts R inside BET, giving BERT. George Herbert was one of the seventeenth-century Metaphysical poets, and also the middle name of D. H. Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: George, the seventeenth-century devotional writer of The Temple, is grouped among the Metaphysical poets with Donne.

clue.text: See it among bridge players one finally doubled

indicators.note: among says one piece goes in among the letters of the other

parts.note: in bridge the players are named by compass points: West, North, East and South
taken as written

indicators.note: finally doubled says the last player's letter at the end appears twice

parts.note: one more bridge player, South, given as S

explanation.surface: Watch the bridge table, where one player ends up doubling the bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' slips the pronoun in after West, and 'finally doubled' gives South twice at the end. 'Doubled' is a bridge bidding term, which is what makes the surface look like a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: To see something happen is to observe it as an onlooker, so both verbs mean to watch with one's own eyes.

clue.text: In writing 2 23 7, the last word for intelligence

definitions.meaning: 2 23 7 is Thomas Edward Lawrence, who wrote Seven Pillars of ..., whose title ends with this word
good sense and sagacity are signs of a sharp mind

explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity and good judgment are a kind of intelligence, and the word ends the title of Lawrence of Arabia's memoir.

clue.text: King Lear, for example

definitions.meaning: eight English kings since the Conquest bore this name
the nonsense poet Lear had this first name, so he is an example of someone so called

explanation.definitionFit: English monarchs from the Confessor to the Eighth bore the name, as did the Victorian nonsense poet Lear.

clue.text: See 1
Prophetic writing in regular letters from farmhouse

indicators.note: regular letters means every other letter is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Prophecies are written in tidy, even script by someone at a farmhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Amos was a herdsman in the Old Testament, which suits the farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book bearing the name of a minor prophet is a piece of prophetic scripture.

clue.text: Drop out of old US university

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A student drops out of an old American university.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to drop or exclude it, as one drops a word from a sentence.

clue.text: A bit of a spur some hero welcomes

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A horseman's spur is something a hero welcomes.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the spiked revolving wheel at the end of a horseman's spur, so a component of one.

clue.text: One who notoriously tangled with keeper and got booked

definitions.text: One who notoriously tangled with keeper and got booked

parts.words: One who notoriously tangled with keeper and got booked
parts.note: reads like a footballer who fouled the goalkeeper and was shown a yellow card, but describes a titled woman in a novel whose affair with her gamekeeper caused a scandal and a famous obscenity trial

explanation.walkthrough: The keeper is a gamekeeper, not a goalkeeper, and 'booked' means put in a book. D. H. Lawrence's novel was tried for obscenity in Britain in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence's titled heroine has a scandalous affair with her gamekeeper Mellors, and the book was famously prosecuted.

clue.text: Old person one identified as Arab national

parts.note: a man is a person
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An elderly person is identified as coming from an Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Oman, the sultanate on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab national.

clue.text: Felt concern about painter, say, like Van Gogh?

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to feel concern is to have cared
a painter is a rope for tying up a boat, so painter is an example of a rope

explanation.surface: Someone worried about an artist who, like Van Gogh, lost part of an ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' looks like an artist next to Van Gogh, but it is a boat's mooring line. Van Gogh cut off part of his own ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Having ears cut short describes Van Gogh, who famously sliced off part of his left ear in 1888.
